newsitem.title: USA: US West Media narrows second-quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: US West Media narrows second-quarter loss.

text.p: U S West Media Group said Tuesday it lost $94 million in its second quarter, an improvement from its loss of $119 million a year earlier.
U S West Media, a wholly owned susidiary of U S West Communications Group, said its revenue increased to $2.3 billion from $2.0 billion a year earlier.
The company said it lost 17 cents a share compared with its year-earlier loss of 21 cents a share.
On an operating basis, U S West Media posted cash flow of $657 million, up from $566 million a year earlier. Cash flow measures income before deducting income tax, depreciation and amortization.
It was U S West's seventh straight quarter of double-digit growth in revenue and operating cash flow, the company said.

"This was another strong quarter -- financially and operationally," said Richard McCormick, chairman of U S West. "This marks the first time our international operations -- including all three lines of business -- were cash-flow positive.
In cable and broadband communications, the company ended the second quarter with almost 5.1 million subscribers, up 3.4 percent from the second quarter 1996.

Revenue from Media Group's domestic cable operations, including its investment in Time Warner Entertainment, increased 6.9 percent to nearly $1.3 billion, while operating cash flow was up 5.8 percent to $402 million.
U S West Media's domestic cellular subscriber base increased 33 percent and its operating cash flow increased 54 percent, to $132 million.
Internationally, its wireless business doubled its subscriber base since the second quarter of 1996. Much of that growth came from One 2 One, the company's joint venture in the United Kingdom.
Media Group's directory publishing business, now called U S WEST Dex, posted revenue growth of 6.6 percent.
